mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment falls below 4% but S&P returns are negative in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production and housing starts increase, it indicates economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both series increase but S&P returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rate leads to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is high but S&P returns are positive in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High CPI indicates inflation, leading to potential monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If CPI is high but S&P returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts are high but S&P returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases and unemployment decreases, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but S&P returns are negative in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production indicates supply strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but S&P returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.
